_provenance.why: Andrew, 2026-10-12: 'Do the meals in the app have a clickable recipe? Most of them are easy enough, but for beef stew and stuff I need more than 2 or 3 lines.'
_provenance.SOURCED: Nothing here is measured from a live cook. Every time, temperature and doneness cue is standard home-cook practice written against each meal's own ingredient list. PLAUSIBLE, NOT MEASURED — the first cook of each meal is the measurement, the same standing as the quantities in fuel-seed-library-expansion.json.
_provenance.rules: Steps name only what the meal's ingredients list holds, plus salt, pepper, oil and water (scripts/checks/fuel-steps.mjs). No quantity that scales with the household is written into a step — the recipe view prints the scaled ingredients above the steps. `minutes` is the clock a step takes on its own; a step done while something else cooks carries none, so a meal's minutes never add up past its total_minutes.
_provenance.shape: slug -> ordered [{ text, minutes? }]. A slug here must be a seeded meal, and every seeded meal must be here: scripts/fuel-seed-sql.mjs refuses to render otherwise.

beef-barley-stew.text: Heat the oven to 325F. Cut the beef chuck into 1-inch cubes, pat them dry with paper towel and season all over with salt and pepper.
Peel the carrots and cut them into thick coins. Dice the onion.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high until it shimmers. Brown the beef in two batches so the pot is never crowded, 3 to 4 minutes a side, until each piece is deep brown. Move it to a plate.
Turn the heat down to medium. Add the onion and a pinch of salt and cook, stirring, until soft and golden at the edges.
Stir in the tomato paste and thyme and cook for 1 minute, until the paste darkens to brick red.
Pour in about a cup of the stock and scrape the bottom of the pot until every brown bit has lifted — that is the flavour of the stew.
Return the beef and its juices, add the rest of the stock and the carrots, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and move to the oven for 1 hour.
Stir in the barley, cover again and return to the oven for 45 to 50 minutes, until the barley is tender and a piece of beef pulls apart with a fork.

If it is thicker than you like, loosen it with a splash of water. Taste and season with salt and pepper, then rest 10 minutes off the heat — it thickens as it stands, and the barley keeps drinking, so add water when you reheat it.

chicken-tortilla-soup.text: Heat the oven to 400F. Cut the tortillas into thin strips, toss with 1 tsp oil and a pinch of salt, and spread them on a sheet pan.
Bake the strips 8 to 10 minutes, tossing once, until golden and crisp. Set aside — they go on at the table.
In a large pot, warm 1 tsp oil over medium heat. Add the cumin and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes with their juice and the stock, and bring to a boil.
Add the chicken thighs whole, season with salt and pepper, lower to a gentle simmer and cover. Cook 15 to 18 minutes, until the thighs read 165F and shred easily.
Lift the chicken onto a board and shred it with two forks.
Drain and rinse the black beans. Add the beans and the shredded chicken to the pot and simmer 5 minutes.
Off the heat, squeeze in the juice of half the limes. Taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls and top with diced avocado, the tortilla strips and a wedge of the remaining lime.

white-chicken-chili.text: Dice the onion. Drain and rinse the cannellini beans.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium. Cook the onion with a pinch of salt for 4 to 5 minutes, until soft and translucent.
Stir in the cumin and cook 30 seconds, then add the green chiles with their liquid.
Add the stock and the chicken breasts, whole. Bring to a boil, then drop to a gentle simmer.
Cover and poach 12 to 15 minutes, until the chicken reads 165F at its thickest point.
While it poaches, mash about a third of the beans with a fork until rough and creamy. This is what thickens the pot.
Lift the chicken out and shred it with two forks.
Stir the mashed beans, the whole beans and the chicken into the pot. Simmer uncovered about 8 minutes, until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Off the heat, squeeze in the lime juice and season with salt and pepper.

italian-wedding-soup.text: Finely grate the parmesan and mince the garlic. Wash the greens (escarole or spinach) and chop them roughly.
In a bowl, mix the turkey, egg, half the parmesan, the garlic, 1/2 tsp salt per pound of meat and a few grinds of pepper with a fork until just combined. Overmixing makes the meatballs tough.
With wet hands, roll the mix into small meatballs — about 3/4 inch, a heaped teaspoon each — and line them up on a plate.
Bring the stock to a boil in a large pot, then lower it to a steady simmer.
Drop the meatballs in one at a time. Simmer 5 minutes without stirring, so they set instead of breaking up.
Stir in the pasta (acini di pepe or orzo) and cook to the packet time, about 8 to 9 minutes, stirring now and then so it does not stick.
Cut a meatball open: no pink in the middle, 165F.
Stir in the greens and cook until wilted — 1 to 2 minutes for spinach, 3 to 4 for escarole.
Taste and season with salt and pepper. Ladle into bowls and finish with the rest of the parmesan.

pork-green-chili.text: Heat the broiler to high with a rack about 6 inches below it. Husk and rinse the tomatillos and put them on a foil-lined sheet pan with the whole poblano peppers.
Broil 5 to 6 minutes a side, until blistered and blackened in spots. Tip a bowl over the poblanos so they steam while you carry on.
While they broil, cut the pork shoulder into 1.5-inch chunks, pat dry and season with salt and pepper. Dice the onion.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high. Sear the pork in batches, about 3 minutes a side, until well coloured. Move it to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion in the fat left behind for 4 minutes, until soft, then stir in the cumin for 30 seconds.
Peel, stem and seed the poblanos. Chop them with the tomatillos and their pan juices — or pulse in a blender — until you have a rough green salsa.
Return the pork to the pot, add the salsa and the stock and scrape the bottom clean. Bring to a simmer.
Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer gently for 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Peel the potatoes, cut them into 3/4-inch cubes and stir them in. Cover and cook 35 to 40 minutes more, until the potato is tender and the pork falls apart when pressed with a spoon.
Break some of the pork up against the side of the pot, squeeze in the lime and taste for salt. Loosen with a splash of water if it is too thick, and rest 5 minutes before serving.

lentil-sausage-soup.text: Slice the sausage into 1/4-inch coins. Peel and dice the carrots, mince the garlic, and strip the kale from its stems and chop the leaves. Rinse the lentils and pick out any stones.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium-high. Cook the sausage 3 to 4 minutes, until the edges have coloured.
Add the carrots, then the garlic and paprika, and stir for a minute or two until fragrant. Do not let the garlic darken.
Add the lentils and the stock and bring to a boil.
Lower to a simmer, partly cover and cook about 20 minutes, until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape.
Stir in the kale and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, until wilted and dark green.
Check the thickness and add a splash of water if it has gone stodgy — lentils keep absorbing as they sit.
Taste before you salt: the sausage and the stock both carry plenty. Season with salt and pepper.

turkey-chili.text: Dice the onion. Drain and rinse the kidney beans and the black beans.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium-high. Add the turkey with 1/2 tsp salt, break it up and cook 6 to 7 minutes, until no pink remains and it starts to colour.
Add the onion and cook 4 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the chili powder and the cocoa and cook 1 minute to toast them.
Add the crushed tomatoes, then swirl about half a can of water around the empty can and pour that in too. Scrape the bottom of the pot.
Add all the beans and bring to a boil.
Lower to a gentle simmer, partly cover and cook 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until a spoon dragged across the bottom leaves a trail.
Taste and season with salt and pepper. Rest 3 minutes before serving.

zuppa-toscana.text: Scrub the potatoes, halve them lengthwise and slice into 1/4-inch half-moons, skin on. Mince the garlic. Strip the kale from its stems and tear the leaves. Slice the sausage into coins.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium-high. Cook the sausage 4 to 5 minutes, until well coloured.
Add the garlic and red pepper flakes and stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in the stock, scrape the bottom of the pot, add the potatoes and bring to a boil.
Simmer uncovered 12 to 15 minutes, until a knife slides through a potato slice but the slices still hold their shape.
Add the kale and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, until tender.
Take the pot off the heat and wait a minute, then stir in the half-and-half. Off the heat is the point: it curdles if it boils.
Taste and season with salt and pepper.

carnitas-bowls.text: Heat the oven to 300F. Cut the pork shoulder into 2-inch chunks and toss with the cumin, oregano, 1 tsp salt per pound of meat and plenty of pepper.
Pack the pork into a Dutch oven in one snug layer. Squeeze over the juice of half the oranges, drop the squeezed halves in, and add water to come halfway up the meat.
Cover and braise for 3 hours, until a chunk falls apart when pressed with a fork.
While it braises, slice the red onion thin and toss it with the juice of the remaining oranges and a big pinch of salt. Leave it at least 30 minutes; it turns pink and loses its bite.
With 25 minutes to go, rinse the rice and cook it: 1 cup rice to 1.25 cups water with a pinch of salt. Boil, cover, turn to the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then rest off the heat, lid on.
Lift the pork onto a sheet pan and shred it into bite-size pieces with two forks. Spoon a few tablespoons of the braising liquid over it.
Broil on high, 6 inches below the element, 4 to 5 minutes, until the edges are crisp and dark. Toss and broil 2 to 3 minutes more. This step is the whole dish.
Build the bowls: rice, carnitas, the pickled onion and chopped cilantro.

cast-iron-ribeye.text: Heat the oven to 450F. Pat the ribeye very dry and season generously with salt and pepper. If you have 20 minutes to let it sit out first, take them.

Scrub the russet potatoes, prick them all over with a fork and microwave on high 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until a knife slides in easily. Put them straight on the oven rack to crisp the skin while everything else cooks.
Toss the broccoli florets with the olive oil, salt and pepper on a sheet pan and roast 12 to 15 minutes, until the tips are charred and the stems tender.

Heat a cast-iron skillet over high until it just smokes. Add 1 tsp oil and lay the ribeye in, away from you. Sear 3 to 4 minutes a side for a 1-inch cut, to 130F in the centre for medium-rare (145F if you want it cooked through), then hold the fat edge against the pan for 30 seconds.
Rest the ribeye on a board for 5 minutes before cutting. Split the potatoes and serve with the broccoli.

chili-lime-thighs.text: Heat the oven to 425F. Cut the sweet potatoes into 3/4-inch cubes — no need to peel — toss with 1 tsp oil and a pinch of salt on a sheet pan, and put them in for an 8-minute head start.
Mix the chili powder, cumin and garlic powder with 1/2 tsp salt, the juice of half the limes and 1 tbsp oil. Turn the chicken thighs in it until coated.
Push the sweet potatoes to one side. Add the thighs and the broccoli florets, tossed in a little oil and salt, in a single layer.
Roast 18 to 20 minutes, until the thighs read 175F and are dark at the edges and the broccoli tips are charred.
Squeeze the remaining lime over the whole pan and rest 2 minutes.

lemon-garlic-salmon.text: Start the rice: rinse it, then put 1 cup rice to 2 cups water in a pot with a pinch of salt. Boil, cover, turn to the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then leave it off the heat with the lid on.
Trim the green beans. Mince the garlic and halve the lemons. Pat the salmon dry and season with salt and pepper.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Lay the salmon in skin-side down and leave it 4 to 5 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the flesh is opaque halfway up. Flip and cook 2 to 4 minutes more, until it reads 145F at the thickest point and flakes with a fork. Move to a plate.
In the same pan, cook the green beans with a pinch of salt and 2 tbsp water, tossing, 4 to 5 minutes, until bright and crisp-tender. Add the garlic for the last 30 seconds.
Squeeze the lemon over the salmon and the beans and serve over the rice.

greek-turkey-bowl.text: Start the rice: rinse it, then put 1 cup rice to 2 cups water in a pot with a pinch of salt. Boil, cover, turn to the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then leave it off the heat with the lid on.
Dice the cucumber and tomato and toss with the juice of half the lemons, a pinch of salt and half the oregano. Set aside.

Mince the garlic. Heat 1 tsp oil in a skillet over medium-high and add the turkey with 1/2 tsp salt per pound and the rest of the oregano. Break it up and cook 7 to 8 minutes, until no pink remains and it starts to colour.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute. Squeeze in the remaining lemon and scrape the pan.
Fluff the rice. Build the bowls: rice, turkey, and the cucumber and tomato on top.

garlic-herb-thighs.text: Halve the baby potatoes, cover with cold salted water, bring to a boil and cook 8 to 10 minutes, until just tender when pierced. Drain.
While they boil, pat the chicken thighs dry and season both sides with the garlic powder, italian seasoning, salt and pepper. Trim the green beans.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook the thighs smooth-side down 5 to 6 minutes, until deep golden, then flip and cook 4 to 5 minutes more, to 175F. Move to a plate.

Put the potatoes cut-side down in the same pan with the green beans and a pinch of salt. Cook 5 to 6 minutes, tossing now and then, until the potatoes are crisp and the beans crisp-tender. A splash of water lifts the stuck bits onto the vegetables.
Return the thighs and their juices to the pan for a minute, then serve.

turkey-burgers.text: Heat the oven to 425F. Scrub the russet potatoes, prick them with a fork and microwave on high 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until a knife slides in. Put them on the oven rack to crisp the skins while everything else cooks.
Toss the broccoli florets with 1 tsp oil and a pinch of salt on a sheet pan and roast about 15 minutes, until charred at the tips.

Mix the turkey with the paprika, garlic powder and 1/2 tsp salt per pound, using your hands and stopping as soon as it comes together. Shape into patties 3/4 inch thick and press a shallow dimple into the centre of each.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a skillet over medium-high. Cook the patties about 5 minutes a side, until well coloured and 165F in the centre.
Rest the patties 2 minutes. Split the potatoes and serve with the broccoli.

blackened-cod.text: Start the rice: rinse it, then put 1 cup rice to 2 cups water in a pot with a pinch of salt. Boil, cover, turn to the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then leave it off the heat with the lid on.
Heat the oven to 450F. Toss the broccoli florets with 1 tsp oil and a pinch of salt on a sheet pan and roast 12 to 14 minutes, until charred at the tips.
Pat the cod or halibut very dry. Rub it with a little oil and coat both sides with the blackening seasoning.

Heat a cast-iron skillet over medium-high until very hot, and open a window — it will smoke. Add 1 tbsp oil and cook the fish 3 to 4 minutes a side, turning once and gently, until the crust is dark and the flesh is opaque, flakes easily and reads 145F.
Serve over the rice with the broccoli.

soy-ginger-stirfry.text: Start the rice: rinse it, then put 1 cup rice to 2 cups water in a pot with a pinch of salt. Boil, cover, turn to the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then leave it off the heat with the lid on.
Slice the chicken breast across the grain into 1/4-inch strips and toss with a teaspoon of the soy sauce. Slice the bell peppers and onion into strips. Grate the ginger and mince the garlic.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok or large skillet over high until it shimmers. Spread the chicken in a single layer, leave it 2 minutes, then stir 2 to 3 minutes more, until no pink remains. Move to a plate.
Add another teaspoon of oil and cook the peppers and onion 3 to 4 minutes, until blistered at the edges but still crisp.
Add the ginger and garlic and stir 30 seconds. Return the chicken, add the rest of the soy sauce and 2 tbsp water, and toss 1 minute, until glossy.

miso-ginger-salmon.text: Start the rice: rinse it, then put 1 cup rice to 2 cups water in a pot with a pinch of salt. Boil, cover, turn to the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then leave it off the heat with the lid on.
Heat the broiler to high with a rack 6 inches below it. Line a sheet pan with foil and oil it lightly.
Whisk the miso, grated ginger, honey and soy sauce together. Pat the salmon dry, set it skin-side down on the pan and spread the glaze over the top.
Toss the trimmed green beans with 1 tsp oil and a pinch of salt and spread them around the salmon.

Broil 8 to 10 minutes, until the glaze is bubbling and dark in spots and the salmon flakes and reads 145F at the thickest point. Watch the last 2 minutes — honey burns fast. If it darkens early, move the pan down a rack.

jerk-thighs.text: Heat the oven to 425F. Cut the sweet potatoes into 3/4-inch cubes, toss with 1 tsp oil and a pinch of salt on a sheet pan, and put them in for an 8-minute head start.
Rub the chicken thighs with the jerk seasoning, 1 tbsp oil and the juice of half the limes.
Add the thighs and the broccoli florets, tossed in a little oil and salt, to the pan in a single layer.
Roast 18 to 20 minutes, until the thighs read 175F and are charred at the edges.
Squeeze the remaining lime over the pan and serve.

turkey-meatballs.text: Start the rice: rinse it, then put 1 cup rice to 2 cups water in a pot with a pinch of salt. Boil, cover, turn to the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then leave it off the heat with the lid on.

Finely dice the onion and mince the garlic. Mix the turkey with the egg, half the onion, half the garlic, the oregano, 1/2 tsp salt per pound and pepper until just combined. Roll into 1.5-inch balls with wet hands.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high. Cook the meatballs 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until coloured on most sides. They are not cooked through yet.
Push them aside and cook the rest of the onion and garlic for 1 minute, then add the crushed tomatoes and a pinch of salt. Cover and simmer on medium-low 10 minutes, until the meatballs read 165F.
While that simmers, boil the green beans in salted water 4 to 5 minutes, until crisp-tender, and drain.
Tear the basil over the pan. Serve the meatballs and their tomato over the rice with the green beans.

tandoori-breast.text: Ahead of time — in the morning or the night before, and not counted in this meal's 45 minutes: mix the yogurt, tandoori seasoning, minced garlic, the juice of half the lemons and 1/2 tsp salt per pound of chicken. Halve any thick chicken breast horizontally so the pieces are even, coat them and refrigerate — an hour at least, a day at most.
Start the rice: rinse it, then put 1 cup rice to 2 cups water in a pot with a pinch of salt. Boil, cover, turn to the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then leave it off the heat with the lid on.
Heat the broiler to high with a rack 6 inches below it. Line a sheet pan with foil and oil it. Shake the excess marinade off the chicken and lay it on the pan.
Broil 7 to 8 minutes a side, until charred in spots and 165F at the thickest point.
While it broils, dice the cucumber and tomato and toss with the remaining lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes, slice it across the grain and serve with the rice and the salad.

chipotle-cod-tacos.text: Shred the cabbage finely and chop the cilantro. Toss both with the juice of half the limes and a good pinch of salt, and leave to soften.
Pat the cod or halibut dry and cut it into 1-inch-wide strips. Season with the chipotle, cumin and salt.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high. Cook the fish 2 to 3 minutes a side, until opaque, flaking and 145F. Squeeze a little more lime over it.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet, 30 seconds a side, until pliable and toasted in spots. Keep them wrapped in a towel.
Fill the tortillas with fish and slaw and serve with the remaining lime in wedges.

flank-chimichurri.text: Make the chimichurri: finely chop the parsley and garlic (or pulse them in a blender) and stir with the vinegar, the olive oil, 1/4 tsp salt and a pinch of pepper. Let it sit.
Pat the flank dry and season both sides generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a grill or a cast-iron skillet on high until it smokes. Sear the flank 4 to 5 minutes a side, to 130F for medium-rare (145F if you want it cooked through), then move it to a board to rest.
While it rests, blister the mini sweet peppers, whole, in the same hot pan with 1 tsp oil and a pinch of salt, 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until charred in spots and soft.
Slice the flank thin across the grain, knife held at an angle. Spoon the chimichurri over and serve the peppers alongside.

smash-burgers.text: Divide the beef into loose balls of about 3.5 oz, two per person, without packing them. Slice the onion paper-thin. Tear the romaine and slice the pickles.
Heat a cast-iron skillet or griddle on high for 3 to 4 minutes, until it smokes. Toast the buns cut-side down for 30 to 60 seconds and set them aside.

Working in batches, set the balls on the dry pan, top each with a pinch of onion and smash flat — 1/4 inch — with a sturdy spatula inside the first 30 seconds. Season with salt and pepper and cook 2 minutes, until the edges are dark and lacy.
Scrape under each patty and flip it onion-side down. Lay the cheddar on top and cook 1 minute more, until it melts.
Stack two patties on each bun with pickles. Dress the romaine with a little oil and a pinch of salt for the side salad.

korean-beef-bowl.text: Start the rice: rinse it, then put 1 cup jasmine rice to 1.25 cups water in a pot with a pinch of salt. Boil, cover, turn to the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then leave it off the heat with the lid on.
Slice the cucumber thin and toss with a pinch of salt. Slice the scallions, keeping whites and greens apart. Stir the gochujang into the soy sauce with 1 tbsp water.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high — no oil needed. Add the beef and the scallion whites, break it up and cook 6 to 7 minutes, until some of it is crisp. Spoon off the excess fat.
Add the gochujang mixture and stir 1 to 2 minutes, until glossy and absorbed.
Fluff the rice and stir the sesame oil through it. Build the bowls: rice, beef, cucumber and the scallion greens.

beef-and-broccoli.text: Start the rice: rinse it, then put 1 cup jasmine rice to 1.25 cups water in a pot with a pinch of salt. Boil, cover, turn to the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then leave it off the heat with the lid on.

Slice the flank thin across the grain — 15 minutes in the freezer first makes it easier — and toss with half the soy sauce and half the cornstarch. Cut the broccoli into small florets, grate the ginger and mince the garlic. Stir the rest of the soy sauce and cornstarch into 1/4 cup water.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok or large skillet over high until it smokes. Working in batches, spread the flank in a single layer, leave it 1 minute, then stir 1 minute more — seared outside, still pink inside. Move to a plate.
Add the broccoli with 1/4 cup water, cover and steam 2 to 3 minutes, until bright green and crisp-tender. Uncover and let the water cook off.
Add the ginger and garlic and stir 30 seconds. Return the flank, pour in the soy and cornstarch mixture and toss 1 minute, until it thickens and coats everything.

pork-tenderloin-apple.text: Heat the oven to 425F. Trim and halve the brussels sprouts and cut the apple into thick wedges. Toss both with half the olive oil, salt and pepper on a sheet pan, sprouts cut-side down.
Pat the pork tenderloin dry and season with salt and pepper. Stir the dijon and the sage together.
Heat the rest of the olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high. Sear the tenderloin about 2 minutes on each of its sides, until coloured all over.
Brush the tenderloin with the dijon and sage. Put the skillet and the sheet pan in the oven and roast 12 to 15 minutes, until the pork reads 145F at its thickest and the sprouts are dark and tender.
Rest the pork 5 minutes, then slice into 1/2-inch medallions and serve over the sprouts and apple.

mustard-pork-chops.text: Pat the pork chops dry and season with salt, pepper and the thyme. Trim the green beans.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Sear the pork 4 to 5 minutes a side, until deep golden and 145F next to the bone; if they are not there yet, give them another minute a side. Stand each one on its fat edge for 30 seconds, then rest them on a plate for 3 minutes.
While the pork cooks, boil the green beans in salted water 4 to 5 minutes, until crisp-tender, and drain.
Pour off all but a film of fat. Add the stock to the hot pan, scrape up the stuck bits and simmer 2 to 3 minutes, until reduced by half.
Off the heat, whisk in the dijon, the butter and any juices from the resting plate until glossy. Taste for salt.
Spoon the pan sauce over the pork and serve the green beans alongside.

garlic-shrimp-skillet.text: Start the rice: rinse it, then put 1 cup jasmine rice to 1.25 cups water in a pot with a pinch of salt and the zest of the lemons. Boil, cover, turn to the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then leave it off the heat with the lid on.
If the shrimp are frozen, thaw them in cold water for 10 minutes. Pat them very dry and salt them. Mince the garlic.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a large skillet on high. Spread the corn in a single layer and leave it 2 to 3 minutes, until charred in spots, then stir and give it 1 minute more. Tip it into a bowl.

Lower the heat to medium-high and melt the butter. Lay the shrimp in a single layer for 2 minutes, until pink underneath, then flip, add the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until opaque and curled into a C.
Off the heat, squeeze in half the lemon juice and toss the corn back in.
Stir the rest of the lemon juice into the rice and serve the shrimp and corn over it.

shrimp-fajitas.text: Heat the oven to 450F. Slice the bell peppers and onion into 1/4-inch strips and toss on a sheet pan with 1 tbsp oil, half the chili powder and a pinch of salt.
Roast 10 minutes, until softened and starting to char.

Pat the shrimp dry and toss with the rest of the chili powder, 1 tsp oil and a pinch of salt. Push the vegetables aside, add the shrimp in a single layer and roast 5 to 6 minutes, until pink and opaque.
Wrap the tortillas in foil and put them in the oven for those last 5 minutes.
Squeeze half the lime over the pan. Serve in the warm tortillas with the rest of the lime in wedges.

chicken-shawarma-bowl.text: Mix half the yogurt with the cumin, coriander, half the garlic (minced), 1/2 tsp salt per pound of chicken and 1 tbsp oil. Coat the chicken thighs — in the morning if you can; it only improves.
Heat the oven to 450F. Spread the thighs on a foil-lined sheet pan and roast 20 to 22 minutes, until 175F and dark at the edges. Finish 2 minutes under the broiler for char.
While the chicken roasts, cook the rice: rinse it, then 1 cup jasmine rice to 1.25 cups water with a pinch of salt. Boil, cover, lowest heat 12 minutes, then rest off the heat.

Make the garlic sauce: stir the rest of the yogurt with the rest of the garlic, grated fine, a pinch of salt and a teaspoon of water. Dice the cucumber, halve the tomatoes and toss them with a pinch of salt.
Rest the chicken 3 minutes and slice it thin. Build the bowls: rice, chicken, cucumber and tomato, garlic sauce over the top.

chicken-piccata.text: Halve each chicken breast horizontally and pound to 1/2 inch between two sheets of wrap. Season with salt and pepper, dredge in the flour and shake off the excess. Trim the woody ends off the asparagus.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Working in batches, cook the chicken about 3 minutes a side, until golden and 165F. Move to a plate.
Add the asparagus to the pan with a pinch of salt and 2 tbsp water and cook, tossing, 3 to 4 minutes, until bright and crisp-tender. Move it to the plates.
Add the stock, the juice of the lemons and the capers to the pan, scrape up the stuck bits and simmer 2 to 3 minutes, until reduced by half.
Off the heat, swirl in the butter until the pan sauce is glossy. Return the chicken and turn it to coat.

arroz-con-pollo.text: Season the chicken thighs with the paprika, salt and pepper. Dice the onion and the bell pepper. Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide, lidded pan over medium-high. Sear the thighs 3 to 4 minutes a side — coloured, not cooked through — and move them to a plate.
Cook the onion and bell pepper in the same pan with a pinch of salt for 4 minutes, until soft. Stir in the rice for 1 minute to coat it.
Add the stock, scrape the bottom of the pan and bring to a boil. Nestle the thighs and their juices on top.
Cover tightly, turn to the lowest heat and cook 18 minutes. Do not lift the lid.
Scatter the peas over the top, cover again and rest off the heat 5 minutes. The rice should be tender and the thighs 175F. Fluff and serve.

honey-soy-mahi.text: Start the rice: rinse it, then put 1 cup jasmine rice to 1.25 cups water in a pot with a pinch of salt. Boil, cover, turn to the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then leave it off the heat with the lid on.
Stir the soy sauce, honey and grated ginger together. Pull the strings off the snap peas. Pat the mahi very dry and salt it lightly.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high. Cook the mahi 3 to 4 minutes, until golden underneath, then flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes more, until opaque, flaking and 145F.
Pour the honey-soy mixture around the fish and let it bubble 1 minute, spooning it over, until syrupy. Move the fish to plates.
Toss the snap peas in the pan with 1 tbsp water for 2 minutes, until bright green and still crisp. Serve everything over the rice with the pan glaze on top.

lemon-crumb-haddock.text: Heat the oven to 425F. Peel the carrots and cut them into sticks about 1/2 inch thick. Toss with half the olive oil and a pinch of salt on a sheet pan and get them roasting while you make the crumb.
Rub the panko, parsley, the zest of the lemons, the rest of the olive oil and a pinch of salt together with your fingers until it feels like damp sand.
Pat the haddock dry and season with salt and pepper. Push the carrots aside, set the fish on the pan and press the crumb onto the top of each piece.
Roast 10 to 12 minutes, until the crumb is golden and the haddock is opaque, flakes easily and reads 145F.
Squeeze the lemon over the fish and the carrots.

sheet-pan-sausage-peppers.text: Heat the oven to 425F. Halve the baby potatoes, quartering any large ones. Slice the bell peppers into strips and the onion into wedges. Cut the sausage into 1-inch pieces.
Toss the potatoes, peppers and onion with the olive oil, italian seasoning, 1/2 tsp salt and pepper on a sheet pan. Spread in one layer, potatoes cut-side down.
Add the sausage, toss, and roast 12 to 13 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender and crisp underneath and the sausage is coloured at the edges and hot through, 165F.

turkey-taco-skillet.text: Toss the cabbage with the juice of half the limes and a pinch of salt. Drain and rinse the black beans.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add the turkey with 1/2 tsp salt per pound, break it up and cook 6 to 7 minutes, until no pink remains and it starts to colour.
Stir in the chili powder for 30 seconds, then add the beans and 1/4 cup water. Simmer 4 to 5 minutes, until saucy rather than soupy.
Squeeze in the remaining lime and taste for salt.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet, 30 seconds a side. Spoon in the turkey and beans and top with the slaw.
